title: Cognitive-memory grounding for NPC forgetting, consolidation and testimony-fidelity parameters
question: What do the peer-reviewed memory-science and cultural-transmission literatures establish about forgetting curves and their dependence on salience and rehearsal, sleep-dependent consolidation, source monitoring and confidence decay, and serial-reproduction/testimony fidelity, so that NOXIA's NPC memory model models real retention and distortion? Concretely: are the state ladder (fresh/consolidated/fading/forgotten), the consolidation strength threshold 0.45 with a ±0.08 confidence change during sleep, the forgetting threshold scaled by resistance = 1 + salience + 0.25·rehearsals, the default confidence 0.65, and the 0.85× speaker-confidence transfer on testimony defensible against measured retention, rehearsal and transmission effects — and does the architecture claim that forgetting/distortion are reasoned mechanisms (perception, time, retrieval, motivation, channel) rather than arbitrary random corruption match the evidence?
why_now: NOXIA-KNOWLEDGE-0001 (2026-10-08) and its stage-1 code (lib/game/knowledge/transmission.ts, npcTestimony.ts, npcRelationalMemory.ts, threeGenerationExperiment.test.ts) are implemented and explicitly move toward a stage-3 end-to-end 'erleben → erinnern → erzählen → weitererzählen → aufzeichnen → vergessen/wiederentdecken' test over simulated generations, and the SSF history/knowledge education content depends on the claim that knowledge without a real channel equals zero. Every retention, consolidation and distortion constant is currently asserted, so grounding them is required before generation-scale results are treated as meaningful.
real_world_anchor: Cognitive and cultural memory science: forgetting-curve and retention-interval empirical work, spacing/rehearsal and salience effects, sleep-dependent memory consolidation, source-monitoring and confidence-accuracy research, and serial-reproduction/transmission-chain studies of narrative distortion and fidelity.
novelty_reason: Not covered by any prior topic. RES-20260828-471FC77C covers need frameworks and relationship trust/affinity dynamics, not memory retention, consolidation, source monitoring or testimony transmission. No previous NOXIA/KUEPER research question addresses the epistemic memory model or its forgetting/distortion constants.
